title: Dad Spoke First
description:
It was a Sunday evening call.

Dad brought it up himself.

'Son. Last time you asked how I was doing — really asked.'

A pause.

'That meant something.'

choices.result_text:
'...Yeah.'

Not many words. But this call ran a little longer before it ended.

{name} hung up and sat still for a while.

choices.text: "Don't mention it. I was just curious."
choices.result_text:
Dad laughed. Quietly.

'A father knows what's behind the "just curious," son.'

That line stayed longer than expected.

title: A Train Ticket and a Medicine Bag
description:
While sorting photos on his phone, he found a train ticket to Changwon from three months ago.
The next photo showed a medicine bag on the table and an apple his father had peeled.

The man who told him not to come had been waiting by the door to take his bag.

choices.text: Save the photos and date in the family album
choices.result_text:
Under the ticket, he wrote: 'The weekend he started medication.'
That day, his father had put another piece of fish in his bowl instead of saying thank you. Even what went unsaid now had a date.

choices.text: Close the photos but keep the ticket
choices.result_text:
He closed the photos without deleting the ticket.
One small date remained as proof that he had actually gone down that weekend.

title: The Time You Did Not Go
description:
He searched his messages for 'medication' and found his mother's text from three months ago.
'Your father started blood pressure medicine.'
Below it sat his reply — 'Okay' — and the empty space where no call had followed.

choices.text: Apologize to your mother for brushing it aside
choices.result_text:
'I treated it too lightly then. I'm sorry.'
After a long pause, his mother replied, 'I know.'
It was a short message, but this time he did not close the conversation first.

He closed the search results.
Other messages rose to the top of the list, but those two words — 'Okay' — remained in the search history.

title: You Came
description:
A late call.

Dad paused before speaking.

'Minjun-ah. That time — you took the train from Seoul in the middle of the night.'

{name} held their breath.

choices.result_text:
'...A father knows what that means.'

A short silence.

'Thank you, Minjun-ah.'

The words stayed. That predawn KTX turned out to have meant something — confirmed for the first time.

choices.text: "I ran because it was you, Dad."
choices.result_text:
Dad laughed softly.

'Right. Because of me.'

A call that had seemed about to end awkwardly found its warmth in that one laugh.
